title: NetworkError and stricter retries
summary: Ky now wraps fetch network failures in a typed NetworkError. It retries only errors it knows, and throws everything else at once.

links.title: Issue #545: Best way to handle fetch errors
PR #842: why the detector is inlined

steps.title: The problem
steps.body:
- Fetch rejects with a raw `TypeError` when the network fails.
- The message depends on the runtime. Chrome says `Failed to fetch`. Firefox says `NetworkError when attempting to fetch resource.`
- Users could not tell a network failure from any other thrown error (#545).
- Before this PR, Ky retried every error that its timeout and HTTP status rules did not reject.
- Ky also retried programming bugs, because a bug is an unknown error too.

links.title: Issue #545: Best way to handle fetch errors
#545: Failed to fetch in the Instagram in-app browser

steps.title: The decision
steps.body:
- Ky wraps each recognized raw network error in a new `NetworkError`.
- By default, Ky retries only `HTTPError`, `TimeoutError` and `NetworkError`. It throws every other error at once.
- sholladay named the cost: a new runtime's unrecognized network error gets no retry. sindresorhus accepted it: "New runtimes don't come along every day."
- `shouldRetry` is the escape hatch for errors that the detector misses.
- Ky inlines the `is-network-error` v1.3.1 detector. Ky keeps zero runtime dependencies.

links.title: PR #842: why the detector is inlined

terms.meaning: The `KyError` subclass that Ky throws when fetch fails at the network level, for example on a DNS failure or a refused connection.
A `TypeError` from fetch whose message is on a known list of per-runtime network messages, such as `Failed to fetch` or `fetch failed`.
The public check that passes when the error is a `NetworkError` instance or has the name `NetworkError`.
The private method that returns the wait in ms before the next attempt, or throws the error to stop retrying.
The user option that overrides the default checks: `true` forces a retry, `false` stops, and `undefined` keeps the defaults.
The standard `Error` property where a `NetworkError` keeps the raw network error from fetch.
An HTTP method in `retry.methods` that Ky may retry, by default `get`, `put`, `head`, `delete`, `options` and `trace`.

steps.title: Parts of the retry path
steps.say: Every Ky attempt runs through `#fetch`. The PR wraps network failures there. It also adds a last check to the retry decision.

notes.text: `Ky.create` starts the first attempt through `#retry`. Every attempt goes through `#fetch`. Only `#fetch` calls `fetch`, the global one or a custom one from options.
When `fetch` rejects, `#fetch` asks `isRawNetworkError` about the error. On a match, `#fetch` throws a `NetworkError` with the original error as `cause`. `#fetch` rethrows any other error unchanged.

`#retry` hands each error to `#retryFromError`. `#retryFromError` asks the retry decision, `#calculateRetryDelay`, for a delay. `#retryFromError` waits for that delay, then calls `#retry` again. If the retry decision throws instead, no retry happens.

The retry decision keeps its earlier checks, such as the retriable method and `shouldRetry`. The PR adds a last check after them. An error that fails the `isNetworkError` guard there is thrown, not retried.
Apps import `NetworkError` and the `isNetworkError` guard from `ky`. The retry decision uses the same public guard.

steps.title: One network failure, then success
steps.say: A GET fails once with `TypeError('Failed to fetch')`, then succeeds. Ky wraps the failure and retries. The GET resolves with the second response.

messages.label: #fetch()
messages.note: `Ky.create` starts the first attempt of `ky.get(url)` here.

messages.label: TypeError: Failed to fetch
messages.note: `#fetch` catches the rejection. `isRawNetworkError` recognizes the message as a raw network error.

messages.label: #calculateRetryDelay(error)
messages.note: `#retry` passes the error through `#retryFromError` to the retry decision.

messages.label: delay (ms)
messages.note: GET is a retriable method. The `NetworkError` passes the `isNetworkError` guard, so the retry decision returns a backoff delay.

messages.label: #fetch()
messages.note: `#retryFromError` waits for the delay. It runs the `beforeRetry` hooks, then calls `#retry` again.

messages.label: 200 Response
messages.note: The `ky.get` promise resolves with this response. The first failure does not reject it.

steps.title: Check
steps.question: With default retry options, which failed first attempt does Ky now retry?

options.text: A GET where `fetch` rejects with `TypeError('Failed to fetch')`.
options.why: `#fetch` wraps the error in a `NetworkError`, and the retry decision retries a `NetworkError` on a GET.

options.text: A GET where `fetch` rejects with `TypeError('Cannot read properties of undefined')`.
options.why: `isRawNetworkError` does not match this message, so the error stays a `TypeError` and the last check throws it.

options.text: A POST where `fetch` rejects with `TypeError('Failed to fetch')`.
options.why: POST is not a retriable method by default, so the method check throws the `NetworkError` before the last check runs.

steps.title: Wrap the fetch failure
steps.say: `#fetch` now catches a failed fetch call. It turns a raw network error into a `NetworkError` before the retry decision sees it.

notes.text: Before, `#fetch` returned the fetch promise without a `catch`. A network failure reached the retry decision as the runtime's own `TypeError`.
The prep before the `try` is unchanged. It clones `this.request` for retries and adds upload progress to the request. An error from this prep skips the new `catch`.
The fetch call now sits inside a `try`. Both branches use `return await`, so a rejected fetch reaches the `catch`. With a bare `return`, the rejection would skip the `catch`.

The `catch` turns a raw network error into a `NetworkError`. It passes `this.request` and keeps the original error in `cause`. Ky rethrows every other error unchanged, such as `TimeoutError` or a `TypeError` from a bug.

steps.title: Recognize a network error
steps.say: `isRawNetworkError` decides which fetch failures count as network errors. It checks the error type first. Then it matches the message against known strings per runtime.

notes.text: This file is a copy of `is-network-error` v1.3.1. `isError` checks `Object.prototype.toString`, so it also accepts an `Error` from another realm. `instanceof Error` would fail there.

`errorMessages` holds the exact messages that mean a network failure. They come from Chrome, Firefox, Safari 16, `cross-fetch`, undici, Bun and Cloudflare Workers. The leading space in the Bun message is intentional.
`isRawNetworkError` first requires a real `Error` with the `name` `TypeError` and a string `message`. For any other value, the function returns `false`.
Safari 17+ uses the generic message `Load failed`. The function counts it only when the error has no stack. Sentry adds its own stack, so the `__sentry_captured__` marker also counts.
Deno messages must start with `error sending request for url`. Chrome messages must be `Failed to fetch`, or `Failed to fetch (<host>)` with the host name.
Every other message must match an entry in `errorMessages` exactly. An unlisted or localized message returns `false`, so `#fetch` rethrows the plain `TypeError`.

steps.title: The NetworkError class
steps.say: `NetworkError` is the typed error that `#fetch` throws. It keeps the request and the original error.

notes.text: `NetworkError` extends `KyError`. It has a literal `name` and a `request` property, the same shape as `TimeoutError`.

The message names the method and the URL: `Request failed due to a network error: <METHOD> <URL>`. `KyError` has no constructor, so `options.cause` reaches `Error`. The original `TypeError` then sits in the standard `cause` property.

steps.title: Retry only known errors
steps.say: The retry decision now retries only the error types it knows. The timeout and `HTTPError` branches return their own delay. A new gate at the end throws everything that is not a `NetworkError`.

notes.text: The limit check rethrows the error when `#retryCount` reaches `retry.limit`. For a network failure, that error is the `NetworkError` from `#fetch`. So `beforeError` hooks see a `NetworkError`, not the raw `TypeError`.
A `ForceRetryError` always gets a delay. Next, the method gate throws when the request method is not a retriable method. This gate runs before any error type check.

`shouldRetry` still runs before the default checks. It now gets the `NetworkError`, because `#fetch` wraps the failure first. `true` forces a retry, `false` throws, and `undefined` falls through to the defaults.
Before, this check threw only when `retryOnTimeout` was off. Any error that no check threw fell through to `#calculateDelay()` at the bottom. Programming bugs got retries too.
A `TimeoutError` now returns its own delay when `retryOnTimeout` is on. Without this early return, the new gate at line 486 would throw it.
The `HTTPError` branch now ends with its own `return`. The Retry-After and 413 rules above it are unchanged. Without this line, the gate at line 486 would throw an error with a retriable status.
The new gate throws every error that is not a `NetworkError`. Only a `NetworkError` gets the default delay from `#calculateDelay()` at line 490. So an unknown error now fails on its first attempt.

steps.title: The public type guard
steps.say: The public `isNetworkError` guard lets callers detect the new error. `isKyError` now accepts it too.

notes.text: `isKyError` now also calls `isNetworkError`. `instanceof KyError` already matched a `NetworkError` from the same realm. So this change only adds the match by name.

`isNetworkError` passes on `instanceof NetworkError` or on the name `NetworkError`. The name check covers a `NetworkError` from another realm, where `instanceof` fails. The other guards in this file use the same pattern.

steps.title: Check
steps.question: What happens when fetch rejects every GET with `TypeError('Failed to fetch')` and the retry limit is 2?

options.text: Fetch runs 3 times, then `beforeError` gets the raw `TypeError` from the last call.
options.why: No, `#fetch` wraps the `TypeError` before the retry decision sees it, so the last error is a `NetworkError`.

options.text: Fetch runs 3 times, then `beforeError` gets a `NetworkError` with the `TypeError` as `cause`.
options.why: `#fetch` wraps each failure, so the gate allows 2 retries before the limit check throws the third `NetworkError`.

options.text: Fetch runs 2 times, then `beforeError` gets a `NetworkError` with the `TypeError` as `cause`.
options.why: No, the limit counts retries, so 2 retries follow the first call for 3 calls in total.

options.text: Fetch runs once, then `beforeError` gets a `NetworkError` because the gate blocks the retry.
options.why: No, the gate throws only errors that are not a `NetworkError`, so this error gets a delay.

steps.title: A bug is not retried
steps.say: A non-network `TypeError` from a custom `fetch` stops at the first attempt. Ky does not wrap it. The retry decision throws it, even with retries left.

messages.label: the same `TypeError`
messages.note: `#fetch` rethrows the error unchanged. It does not become a `NetworkError`.

messages.label: `#calculateRetryDelay(error)`
messages.note: The count is 0 of 2. GET is a retriable method.

messages.label: throws the `TypeError`
messages.note: The error is not a timeout, an `HTTPError` or a `NetworkError`. The gate at the end of the retry decision throws it.

messages.label: raw `TypeError` after 1 call
messages.note: Before, the old fall-through retried any error. The same request made 3 calls.

steps.title: Tests for unknown TypeErrors
steps.say: Two new tests pin the bug case. Without `shouldRetry`, Ky makes 1 call. With `shouldRetry: () => true`, Ky still retries up to the limit.

notes.text: The retry options allow 2 retries with no wait. The custom `fetch` throws a `TypeError` with a message that `isRawNetworkError` does not know.
The test expects the raw `TypeError` after exactly 1 call. It fails if the gate at the end of the retry decision goes away.
This test uses the same failing `fetch`, plus `shouldRetry: () => true`. This is the escape hatch for errors that Ky does not recognize.
Ky makes 3 calls: 1 initial and 2 retries. Then it throws the raw `TypeError`, not a `KyError`. `isKyError` returns `false` for this error.

steps.title: POST is wrapped, not retried
steps.say: A network failure on POST still becomes a `NetworkError`. Ky does not retry it, because POST is not a retriable method.

notes.text: `ky.post` allows 2 retries. The custom `fetch` throws `TypeError('Failed to fetch')`. `isRawNetworkError` matches that message.
Ky throws a `NetworkError` after 1 call. The wrapping in `#fetch` does not depend on the method. The method check at the start of the retry decision throws the error before the `isNetworkError` gate.

steps.title: Wrapping with timeout disabled
steps.say: With `timeout: false`, a network failure still becomes a `NetworkError`. This test guards the `await` that the PR added to the `timeout: false` branch of `#fetch`.

notes.text: `timeout: false` makes `#fetch` call `options.fetch` directly, without the `timeout()` race. The custom `fetch` throws a raw network error.
The test expects a `NetworkError` with the `TypeError` in `cause`. Without the added `await`, the rejection would skip the `catch` in `#fetch`. Then this test would fail.

steps.title: The guard matches by name
steps.say: `isNetworkError` passes an error by class or by `name`. The `name` match also passes errors that Ky did not create.

notes.text: A browser `DOMException` named `NetworkError`, or an app class with that name, passes this guard and `isKyError`. The type then promises a `request` property that such an error may not have. If such an error reaches the retry decision, the gate at `Ky.ts:486` lets it retry.

steps.title: A client bug becomes NetworkError
steps.say: Real undici reports this client bug as `TypeError('fetch failed')`, a message that `isRawNetworkError` matches. On PUT, Ky still retries the bug. The new readme text says that programming bugs are thrown at once.

notes.text: The body `sup` does not match the header `content-length: 0`. This is a bug in the caller, not a network failure. The request uses POST, so the method gate stops a retry.
The raw `TypeError` is now the `cause` of the `NetworkError`. So the undici code moves from `error.cause.code` to `error.cause.cause.code`.

steps.title: Other errors Ky does not wrap
steps.body:
- A thrown value that is not an `Error`. Before, Ky retried it.
- An `AbortError` from a user abort. It now skips the backoff. Before, `delay` rejected on the aborted signal.
- An error from a custom `fetch` whose name is not `TypeError`, such as node-fetch `FetchError`. Before, Ky retried it.
- A `TypeError` that `isRawNetworkError` does not match: an unlisted runtime message, or a Safari `Load failed` with a stack and no Sentry marker. Before, Ky retried it.
- An error thrown while the body is read, such as undici `terminated` in `.json()`. This happens after `#fetch` returns, so its `catch` does not wrap the error.

steps.title: Check
steps.question: A GET with a custom `fetch` throws a node-fetch `FetchError`: what does Ky do, and how do you get retries?

options.text: Ky throws the raw `FetchError` after one call. A `shouldRetry` that returns `true` for it restores retries.
options.why: `shouldRetry` runs before the gate that throws the unwrapped `FetchError`.

options.text: Ky wraps it in a `NetworkError` and retries it up to `limit`. No change is needed.
options.why: `isRawNetworkError` requires the name `TypeError`, so Ky does not wrap a `FetchError`.

options.text: Ky retries the raw `FetchError` up to `limit`, then throws it. No change is needed.
options.why: That was the behavior before this PR, when every unknown error fell through to a retry.

options.text: Ky throws the raw `FetchError` after one call. A `shouldRetry` that returns `undefined` restores retries.
options.why: `undefined` falls through to the default checks, and the last gate still throws the `FetchError`.

steps.title: What to check
steps.body:
- A `catch` that checks `instanceof TypeError` now misses wrapped network failures. The `beforeRetry` workaround from #545 now stops network retries, because the `is-network-error` package accepts only errors named `TypeError`. The PR does not mark either change as breaking.
- When `isRawNetworkError` misses a network failure, Ky throws the error with no retry and no log. Check if `shouldRetry` is enough as the only escape hatch.
- The readme says Ky throws programming bugs at once. On Node, a `content-length` mismatch still becomes a `NetworkError`. Ky retries it on retriable methods.
- `isNetworkError` can give the wrong answer. It passes a `DOMException` named `NetworkError`, which has no `request`. It returns false for an undici `terminated` error during a body read, because Ky wraps only errors thrown inside `#fetch`.
- `NetworkError.message` holds the full URL, as the `HTTPError` and `TimeoutError` messages do. Tokens in the query string may reach logs.

steps.title: In short
steps.body:
- `#fetch` wraps a raw network error in a `NetworkError`. The original error stays in `cause`.
- `isRawNetworkError` checks the message against a fixed list per runtime. Ky does not wrap or retry an error with an unlisted message.
- For a retriable method, the retry decision retries a `NetworkError`, a `TimeoutError` with `retryOnTimeout`, and an `HTTPError` with a retriable status.
- Ky throws any other error on the first attempt. Before, the retry decision retried these errors too.
- `shouldRetry` runs before these checks. It returns `true` to retry an error that Ky does not know.

steps.title: Also changed
steps.body:
- `readme.md` documents network retries. It also adds a `NetworkError` section.
- Doc comments only: `source/errors/HTTPError.ts`, `source/errors/KyError.ts`, `source/types/hooks.ts`, `source/types/options.ts`, `source/types/retry.ts`.
- `test/hooks.ts` fakes failures with `TypeError('Failed to fetch')`. Ky no longer retries the old fake errors, so the tests needed the change.
- `test/retry.ts` adds the `NetworkError` tests. `test/memory-leak.ts` expects `NetworkError` instead of `TypeError`.
- `source/index.ts` exports `NetworkError` and `isNetworkError`. `source/core/Ky.ts` and `source/utils/type-guards.ts` add imports.
